plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan Rattlesnake AGI #1 Yoakum County, Texas
ama_definition: A half-mile buffer around the modeled plume at end of injection (2036), which also contains the 2041 plume, covering a 14-year monitoring period; a revised plan is due by 2036 (p42).
mma_definition: The stabilized plume after modeled density drift (about 2,177 acres) plus a buffer of at least half a mile (p41-42).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None are rated likely. Surface equipment and the AGI well (plus ten deep penetrations in the MMA) get most of the monitoring; faults, the confining layer and seismicity are rated unlikely or very low risk (p44-53).
baseline_summary: Operational baseline of injection volumes and pressures taken from SCADA, plus one pre-expansion groundwater sample from the operator's on-site water well analyzed by a third-party lab (p59-60).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 of the following year; records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data. The appended TRRC permit requires monthly monitoring of injection pressure and volume reported annually on Form H-10 (p64, p67, p77).

rows.detail: Volumetric flow meter on the injected stream, flows compiled quarterly; composition from a continuous analyzer or representative sampling upstream of the meter, averaged quarterly. Any future stream gets its own meter.
rows.location: AGI injection line upstream of the wellhead; separate meter for any future stream
rows.evidence_quote: Flow meters will be continuously operated except for maintenance and calibration.

rows.detail: SCADA and the plant control system continuously record injection volume, pressure, temperature and composition at the AGI well; wellhead shut-in valve on high/low pressure; data reviewed by qualified staff.
rows.location: Rattlesnake AGI #1 wellhead and plant surface equipment
rows.trigger_or_response: Data outside limits or deviation suggesting fault/seal pathway: alert, review by personnel, shut in well if needed; M3.0+ seismic event triggers review of volumes and pressures.
rows.evidence_quote: Stakeholder continuously monitors and collects injection volumes, pressures, temperatures and gas composition data, through their SCADA systems

rows.detail: Pressure gauge on the casing annulus of the AGI well; a change in annulus pressure is treated as a sign of a possible leak.
rows.trigger_or_response: Change in annulus pressure indicates possible leak; reviewed under response procedures.
rows.evidence_quote: a pressure gauge on the casing annulus. A change of pressure on the annulus would indicate the presence of a possible leak.

rows.detail: Annual MITs under TRRC rules to confirm the AGI well and wellhead hold pressure.
rows.trigger_or_response: Failed MIT: well isolated immediately and leak mitigated.
rows.evidence_quote: Mechanical integrity tests (“MITs”) performed annually would also indicate the presence of a leak.

rows.detail: Daily field inspections of the plant and AGI well, looking at gauges, monitors and leak signs such as vapor plumes and ice.
rows.location: 30-30 Facility and Rattlesnake AGI #1 well site
rows.trigger_or_response: Vapor clouds or ice found: corrective action taken.
rows.evidence_quote: field personnel conduct daily visual field inspections of gauges, monitors and leak indicators such as vapor plumes.

rows.detail: All field personnel wear H2S monitors alarming at 5 ppm; H2S serves as the proxy for CO2 leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, check monitors, secure facility and mitigate leak; CO2 release quantified from operating conditions.
rows.evidence_quote: all Stakeholder field personnel are required to wear H2S monitors, which trigger the alarm at 5 ppm H2S.

rows.detail: Fixed H2S detectors (10 ppm alarm) around plant and well; fixed H2S and CO2 monitors at the well site; mobile CO2/H2S readings near penetrating wells in the AMA at least quarterly.
rows.location: Plant, AGI well site, any new meter; penetrating well sites within the AMA
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, verify monitor, secure facility and mitigate leak.
rows.evidence_quote: At the well site, H2S and CO2 concentrations will be monitored continuously with fixed monitors

rows.detail: The operator's on-site water well (119 ft) sampled yearly and analyzed by a third-party lab for pH, TDS, inorganic and organic carbon, density, temperature and standard parameters.
rows.location: One groundwater well on the 30-30 facility property (State Well ID 482963)
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant change from baseline: investigate whether CO2 leaked to the USDW.
rows.evidence_quote: sampling the well on the facility property and analyzing the sample with a third‐party laboratory on an annual basis

rows.detail: Operator will install its own seismic station near the well, tied into TexNet, in service about six months after installation starts; plan also cites one-time USGS and TexNet catalog review.
rows.location: General area of the Rattlesnake AGI #1 well
rows.trigger_or_response: Event of M3.0 or greater: review injection volumes and pressures for signs of leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: Stakeholder plans to install a seismic monitoring station in the general area of the Rattlesnake AGI #1 well.

rows.detail: Existing 3D seismic (about 9 square miles) used to map faults; no repeat seismic.
rows.evidence_quote: Faults were interpreted from roughly 9 square miles of 3D seismic

rows.detail: Atmospheric CO2 and H2S measured with mobile gas monitors at penetrating well sites within the AMA, recorded at least quarterly; also measured at the AGI well site.
rows.location: AGI well site and identified penetrations within the AMA
rows.evidence_quote: At penetrating well sites, Stakeholder will similarly measure atmospheric concentrations of CO2 and H2S using mobile gas monitors.

rows.detail: Corrosion control program checked by periodic inspection of the system, analysis of liquids collected from the line, and inspection of cathodic protection.
rows.evidence_quote: The effectiveness of the internal and external corrosion control program is monitored through the periodic inspection of the system

rows.detail: H2S monitoring during drilling of offset wells, listed as the method for leakage from future wells.
rows.evidence_quote: H2S Monitoring during offset drilling operations

rows.detail: Subpart W methods for equipment leaks between meter and wellhead; any detected release calculated from pressure, flow rate, opening size and duration; blowdowns go to flare.
rows.location: Surface equipment between flow meter and wellhead
rows.evidence_quote: Calculation methods from subpart W will be used to calculate CO2 emissions from equipment located on the surface

notes: Plan is titled for the Rattlesnake AGI #1 well serving the 30-30 plant. The quarterly mobile CO2/H2S readings near penetrating wells, which the plan calls 'atmospheric monitoring', are coded under fixed_gas_detectors per the guide's scheduled-handheld-survey rule, not atmospheric_co2. Plan says MITs are annual; the appended TRRC permit only requires an annulus pressure test before injection and after workovers (p77). Seismic station frequency not stated. Monitoring runs for the 17-year injection period plus a proposed 5-year post-injection period (p56). Not EOR; no CO2 produced (p62).
